title: Intel® 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual — Combined Volumes: 1, 2A, 2B, 2C, 2D, 3A, 3B, 3C, 3D, and 4
edition: Order Number 325462-078US, December 2022
review_note: UNRESOLVED EDITION MISMATCH (see docs/REFERENCE_INDEX.md and PLAN.md D24/D25): this is a genuinely live, fetched, hash-verified copy of Intel's combined four-volume SDM at a real cdrdv2-public.intel.com URL -- but its content is Order Number 325462-078US, December 2022 (5,060 pages, confirmed by pdftotext page-break count), NOT the 325462-092US, December 2024 edition that references/intel_sdm/**'s own frontmatter was derived from (that corpus, and its frontmatter side-table docs/intel_sdm_frontmatter.json, are -092US-relative -- labelled as such there). A live copy of the exact -092US edition could not be located: the same stable URL currently serves -078US; Intel's post-2024 individual-volume PDFs (e.g. 253665-sdm-vol-1-dec-24.pdf, order 253665-086US) belong to a restructured ten-volume scheme with different page numbering and are not this document. No fabricated URL or hash has been substituted -- this entry pins exactly what was actually fetched and hashed on fetched_date. FIXED 2026-08-27 (adversarial review): the 267 migrated citations previously carried pp=/mp= page-range locators derived mechanically from the -092US frontmatter, presented with no signal that they were unverified against these -078US pinned bytes -- two years of revisions move page numbers by hundreds, so pp=/mp= were systematically wrong, not merely unverified. Rather than continue documenting that gap, pp=/mp= were stripped from all 267 citations (scripts/check_references.py's pdf-locator grammar now treats them as optional): each citation now reads only vol=/instr=|sec=/part=, which resolve by lookup in any edition and remain accurate. The -092US page data itself is not lost -- it survives in docs/intel_sdm_frontmatter.json for whoever eventually sources the genuine -092US PDF (or decides to accept -078US as authoritative and re-derive pp= from it). CORRECTION: an earlier version of this note claimed 'max cited page_end is 3201' as evidence the page_count range check (pp end <= 5060) could not catch the edition drift; that number was itself never independently verified and was wrong -- the actual maximum was 2,873, still comfortably under 5,060, so the substance of the point (the range check cannot detect this class of drift regardless of the exact max) is unaffected by the correction. Recorded here as a caution: an unverified number in an honesty note is worse than no number, because it looks verified.

title: Semihosting for AArch32 and AArch64
edition: ARM DUI 0471 / Release 2020Q4
review_note: Defines AArch64 semihosting trap mechanism using HLT #0xF000, operation numbers including SYS_EXIT (0x18), and parameter block format with extended reason ADP_Stopped_ApplicationExit (0x20026) for clean QEMU process exit.

title: Procedure Call Standard for the Arm® 64-bit Architecture (AArch64)
edition: 2025Q4 release (ARM IHI 0055)
review_note: Defines the AArch64 Procedure Call Standard (ARM IHI 0055 / abi-aa), covering general-purpose register usage (argument registers X0-X7, return values X0-X1, callee-saved registers X19-X28, frame pointer X29, link register X30) and 16-byte stack pointer alignment rules.
